newsitem.title: MALTA: EU leader optimistic of Malta meeting.
newsitem.headline: EU leader optimistic of Malta meeting.

text.p: Arab countries intend to separate Middle East peace problems from the work of a European and south Mediterranean foreign ministers' meeting in Malta this month, the EU council of ministers chairman said on Wednesday.

Hans van Mierlo, who is also Dutch foreign minister, said: "The Arab countries, despite the enormous problems in the Middle East, are really willing to make a success of this conference and intend separating it as much as possible from the problems in the Middle East peace process."
Van Mierlo, on a brief visit to Malta, told a news conference: "I think, on the other hand, that if the conference is a success, it can have a positive influence on the Middle East peace process."
Representatives of the Palestinian Authority and Arab states and a large Israeli delegation are among those due to attend the April 15 and 16 meeting in Malta.
It is to follow-up and assess progress since the 1995 Barcelona conference that agreed to forge an EU-Med partnership between the 27 participants.
The Arab League on Monday decided to stop multilateral contacts with Israel on the peace process in protest at Israel's work on a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.
Arab states on Tuesday said they would still attend the Malta meeting, aimed at improving cooperation between the EU members and Mediterranean non-members.

Van Mierlo had talks with Maltese Foreign Minister George Vella. The EU official, who has visited Morocco, Algeria and Tunisia, was later to visit Egypt and Turkey over preparations for the conference.
